speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They can cause tensions between people who feel differently about and who identify with different sides of the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And we in Singapore have been affected by these forces as well.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We see in particular a divide in the reactions between the Malay/Muslim community on the one side and the Jewish and Christian communities on the other side.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Many in the Malay/Muslim community see the injustice in what is happening in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Jewish community meanwhile feels deeply the pain inflicted by Hamas’ act of terror on 7 October 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are sections of the Christian community who feel that any attack on Israel is an attack on Christianity – while not all Christians feel that way, there are some who feel that way and have expressed those views.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Other communities may also empathise with one side of the conflict more than the other.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Deeply held feelings can also result in words or actions that offend other communities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In this context, let me also say something about protests.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen how tensions have boiled over in many countries.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In Berlin, pro-Palestinian protestors have clashed with the police, with hundreds of people arrested.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At United States (US) universities, exchanges between different groups of pro-Israel and pro-Palestine student protestors have become increasingly acrimonious.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Students on both sides have faced harassment and assault.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ironically, some of the leading US universities are beginning to say that freedom of expression does not mean that one can say or do anything one wants.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What we see happening in many places overseas is that the protests have often become violent.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: People occupy buildings, prevent others from going about their daily businesses, cause significant disamenities and disruption to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And often, that leads to damage and harm.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They may start off well-intentioned, led by honest, idealistic people.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I mean, people often say, "What's wrong with protests, expression of views?" And I can understand that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Often, people genuinely feel the need and they are not violent people.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But what happens is that when there are these protests, they often get infiltrated, as we can see from elsewhere, by others with their own agendas.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These others who infiltrate these protests often try and engineer violence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The New York Times and other media outlets have run stories on what is happening in the US right now.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Mayor of New York has reportedly criticised outside agitators for being on campus grounds training and co-opting the protests.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He was concerned with, and I quote, “young people…being influenced by those who are professionals at radicalising children”.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The New York Times ran an article, quoting a student saying that a big part of the protests was people coming in from the general Los Angeles area and putting on a demonstration that caused widespread disruption.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These are on the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) campuses.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are also reports which, on the other hand, deny that outsiders have been significantly involved.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think it is difficult to know the true facts, but looking at protests – and we have been studying them, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka, other places – I think it is fair to say, often, there is a group which has legitimate aims, wants to be peaceful, but there are often others who use these events where people gather, to then engineer violence and put the police on the defensive, and try and egg the police on, to try and engage in forcibly preventing acts of violence, and then, it escalates.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Likewise, our own view is that: if we allow protests on this issue, initially, it may be peaceful, but over time, as the protests take a life of their own, there could be some violence, breach of the peace and law, occupying of buildings in Singapore; we are no different from other places.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We should accept that individuals who engage in offensive or violent conduct, however, are a very small minority in our society and I suspect in many other places too.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We in Singapore have not had many serious incidents pitting one racial or religious group against another.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Most Singaporeans understand the importance of safeguarding our social cohesion, and the value of mutual respect and tolerance.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Even where views on the conflict have differed, people in Singapore have been relatively measured and rational in the way we have approached the issues.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Beyond the law, we have to work actively, and we do work actively, on strengthening our social compact by building mutual trust and understanding across our ethnic and religious communities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At the leadership level, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) facilitate platforms where senior religious and community leaders engage with one another frequently.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The platforms include the National Steering Committee on Racial and Religious Harmony, as well as the Racial and Religious Harmony Circles in every constituency.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At the people-to-people level, MCCY provides support for inter-faith and inter-ethnic initiatives that bring different communities together, including dialogues which encourage mutual understanding and respectful interactions across different communities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Foreign embassies and diplomatic staff in Singapore enjoy diplomatic immunity under the law, unless they waive it.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Amongst other things, this means that they enjoy immunity from our criminal jurisdiction.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Nevertheless, MHA shared our concerns with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) when the post was put up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: MFA then engaged the Israeli Embassy on the post and asked that it be taken down.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As Members would know, the Embassy took down the post immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members will remember what I said in public – that the post was completely unacceptable.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He apologised for the post having been put up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He said it was wrong for the post to have been put up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And he said that this would never happen again.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I pointed out to him that embassies are entitled to have their point of view.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But where what has been said affects Singapore, in this case the harmony and safety within Singapore, especially the security as well of our minority communities, we have to step in.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Posts like what the Embassy put up have the potential to create tension between our Jewish and Muslim communities, and may also put our Jewish community, in particular, at risk.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Police received a report on the post.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members would understand the Israeli Embassy’s actions are covered by the principle of sovereign immunity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with the Minister's statement that such offensive posts put all communities at risk, including our Jewish community here.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second supplementary question is how do we ensure, assuming diplomatic immunity in future cases are waived, that due process in open court can be dealt with sensitively, given that it may play out in the court of public opinion and escalates certain tensions or emotions on the ground?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the first question, is he referring to posts by any member of public or is he referring to posts by embassies?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If it is by members of the public, of course, we have a variety of powers, under different pieces of legislation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is the Online Criminal Harms Act, the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act, the Broadcasting Act.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you look at the different pieces of legislation, depending on what infringements there are, there are powers to block access.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are powers under the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act to even issue a restraining order.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, you would not be able to, for example, issue directly an order to the embassy to remove a posting on its website.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You could look at more general steps, like blocking entire access to the platform, but that would be a very high signature step and I think we need to be careful.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they refuse, and I do not want to be going too much into hypotheticals, but for example, if they refuse to take it down, then there are the usual diplomatic steps that one country can take vis-à-vis another country.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But you got to assess the nature of the infringement, as it were, and how you calibrate it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It can be calibrated to how you give access or how many people you allow in the embassy to be in Singapore or you ask some to leave, in an extreme case; you have seen those sorts of things happen.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Even when they are spying you cannot charge them, let alone when they put up a post.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will have to act in accordance with international law but within that framework, we will have to see what is possible to do.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the Member's second question, Sir, it is, I think, very hypothetical that any embassy would waive diplomatic immunity and allow another country to charge them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It has happened infrequently, but it is extremely hypothetical.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What countries will normally say is, "Look, we will deal with the person by sending him back and then deal with him in our own way".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members may recall the case of Mr Ionescu from Romania.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They can always apply for it to be heard in camera, but they have got to show public interest, I think.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Short of taking action if the embassy waives immunity, there are other steps that can be taken under various pieces of legislation as well.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand, hon Minister, that there are limitations in the directions that could be provided.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, was there any consideration, given the sensitive nature of the post, to request for a clarification, given that the embassy's post took the original video out of context, as well as perhaps an apology as many in the community, from various communities, were quite upset about the post?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have one additional supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Did the Israeli Embassy or any other embassies take any other actions to state their case in the Israel-Hamas conflict since 7 October 2023 and what actions has the Government taken in response?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second question, as far as I know, the embassy has not said anything to me, neither has the ambassador said anything to me, beyond what I have said to Members.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member may wish to ask the MFA for any other clarifications.
